strengths: Well-motivated framework that coherently addresses two genuine limitations of VLA-based driving: lack of exploration and sparse supervision. The unified approach using world modeling for both dense supervision and exploration signals is conceptually elegant.

Strong empirical results on NAVSIM benchmark (PDMS 93.7 with best-of-N, 90.4 without), achieving state-of-the-art performance with only single-view camera input while competitors use multi-view/multi-sensor setups.

Comprehensive experimental validation with systematic ablation studies (Tables 3-4) demonstrating the contribution of RGB/depth supervision (+2.3 PDMS) and reward components. Figure 3 effectively shows entropy-based novelty captures trajectory diversity better than L2 error.
Technically sound and reproducible: detailed hyperparameters, promised code release, clear two-stage training strategy, and principled architectural choices (omni-attention, MAGVIT-v2 tokenizer).
Practical qualitative validation: Figure 4 demonstrates concrete safety-critical failure corrections (collisions, pedestrian risks, traffic violations) that pure imitation learning fails to resolve.
Sensible safety design: Safety-gated reward (Eq. 7) ensures exploration only on safe, high-performing trajectories, mitigating risk of harmful discovery.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Dense world modeling (DriveVLA-W0, UniDrive-WM), uncertainty-based exploration (curiosity-driven RL), and GRPO are all known techniques. The contribution is primarily in their combination rather than fundamental innovation.

Modest RL improvements when best-of-N post-processing is excluded: Stage 1 achieves PDMS 88.5, Stage 2 reaches 90.4 (+1.9 points). Ablation Table 4 reveals image reward contributes only +0.03 points while PDMS reward drives +1.7 points, suggesting the image-based exploration signal provides marginal benefit.

Heavy reliance on post-processing: The headline result (93.7) depends on best-of-N trajectory selection (N=6), which adds ~3.3 PDMS points and is orthogonal to the RL training pipeline. Unclear if this post-processing is applied to baselines for fair comparison.

Weak generalization to open-loop evaluation: On nuScenes, only Stage 1 applied (Stage 2 requires closed-loop metrics). L2 error (0.44m) underperforms OpenDriveVLA (0.33m) and AutoVLA (0.40m), suggesting method benefits from NAVSIM's closed-loop nature and may not generalize well.

Pseudo ground-truth depth: Depth maps from Metric3D pre-trained monocular depth estimation, not actual sensor data. Introduces systematic errors that propagate through supervision and exploration signals. Limited analysis of this dependency's impact on results.

Insufficient world model quantitative evaluation: No metrics (LPIPS, SSIM, FVD) for RGB/depth generation quality. Only qualitative results (Fig. 6) with acknowledged fine-grained detail degradation. Unclear how generation quality impacts exploration signal reliability.

Limited exploration signal analysis: Only one qualitative example (Fig. 3) demonstrating entropy's superiority. Lacking systematic analysis of when/why entropy reliably measures out-of-distribution-ness. No sensitivity analysis for safety threshold δ=0.9 or exploration weight λ=0.5.

Computational efficiency not addressed: Stage 2 requires generating future images for each sampled trajectory (G=8) and computing entropy over all tokens. No timing comparisons or practical deployment cost analysis provided.

Missing failure analysis and robustness discussion: No discussion of failure modes, scenarios where uncertainty-based exploration hurts, or cases where safety-gating fails. Only positive examples presented.

Theoretical justification limited: Connection to exploration literature (curiosity-driven learning, intrinsic motivation) not established. Claim that 'uncertainty reflects distance to entire training distribution' supported by only one example rather than principled analysis.

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear articulation of behavior cloning limitations and RL challenges in autonomous driving
Strong empirical results on NAVSIM achieving state-of-the-art PDMS of 93.7 and EPDMS of 88.8, representing substantial improvements over prior work
Coherent unified approach addressing two complementary limitations through dense world modeling as both supervision and exploration signal
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including thorough ablation studies, analysis of exploration bonus behavior, qualitative safety improvements, and multi-benchmark validation
Solid technical soundness with practical design choices (entropy-based uncertainty, safety gating mechanism)
Good reproducibility support through detailed hyperparameters and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—combines existing techniques (dense supervision, world models, GRPO) without significant novel insights; joint trajectory+image generation established in prior work (DriveVLA-W0, UniDrive-WM)

Unclear source of performance improvements with no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; gap between ExploreVLA† (93.7) and DriveVLA-W0† (93.0) is only 0.7 points potentially within noise; single runs reported
Best-of-N (N=6) strategy for headline result introduces 6× computational overhead not discussed; makes improvements hard to attribute to the proposed method versus sampling

World model quality concerns including acknowledged degradation in fine-grained details (Fig. 6) but lack of quantitative evaluation (PSNR/SSIM); unclear how poor image quality affects exploration signal reliability

Exploration signal validity not rigorously validated—assumes visual uncertainty indicates beneficial novelty but doesn't distinguish between rare behaviors versus model failure/hallucination; high uncertainty could indicate OOD regions or model breakdown

Weak generalization: nuScenes evaluation only uses Stage 1 without RL (suggesting Stage 2 doesn't help); L2 error (0.44m) underperforms OpenDriveVLA (0.33m), questioning whether gains are NAVSIM-specific

Missing empirical validation of core assumptions: no comparison with simpler exploration baselines (random, disagreement-based), no analysis of how often safety gate activates or what novel strategies are discovered
Limited scope with single front-view camera and NAVSIM-only results for RL; external dependency on pre-trained Metric3D estimator affects reproducibility

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation addressing two genuine limitations of VLA-based driving: exploration brittleness and supervision sparsity
Strong empirical results: SOTA on NAVSIM (93.7 PDMS, 88.8 EPDMS) using only single-camera input while surpassing multi-sensor baselines; competitive on nuScenes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablation studies, cross-benchmark validation, and qualitative analysis showing safety improvements (collision avoidance, pedestrian safety)
Coherent unified framework elegantly combining dense world modeling with uncertainty-based exploration; entropy-based novelty measure is intuitive and theoretically natural
Well-presented paper with clear progression, informative visualizations, and reproducible technical details; promises code release
Practical efficiency gain through single-camera architecture while achieving SOTA performance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: dense world modeling auxiliary supervision (DriveVLA-W0, UniDrive-WM), entropy-based intrinsic rewards, and GRPO are all established techniques; main contribution is their integration rather than fundamental innovation

Insufficient analysis of exploration mechanism: Fig. 3 only shows surface-level correlation; missing analysis of what novel behaviors are discovered, whether unsafe trajectories are properly filtered, and comparison with alternative novelty measures (count-based, ensemble disagreement, etc.)

Depth map acquisition inadequately addressed: pseudo-labels from pre-trained monocular estimator, not ground truth; no analysis of depth estimation error propagation; monocular depth scale ambiguity not discussed; missing ablation on depth quality impact

Incomplete ablation studies: no sensitivity analysis on key hyperparameters (λ=0.5, δ=0.9, group size G=8); restrictive safety threshold δ=0.9 unjustified; no ablation on GRPO epochs (fixed at 5); missing alternative world model architecture comparisons
Best-of-N (N=6) reporting obscures improvements: 93.7 vs. 90.4 represents 3.3 point gap; comparison fairness with baselines unclear; makes it difficult to isolate core contribution

Limited generalization: single front-view camera only; only two datasets tested; nuScenes results use only Stage 1 without RL, limiting exploration effectiveness claims; no real-world evaluation or diverse scenario testing

World model generation quality degradation not addressed: Fig. 6 shows visible fine-detail loss (traffic lights, branches) potentially important for safety; no quantitative generation metrics (LPIPS, SSIM); unclear if generation or auxiliary supervision drives improvements

Computational cost not discussed: 4×H200 GPUs required for training; no computational cost comparison with baselines; inference time with image generation not reported; value proposition relative to complexity unclear

Missing failure analysis: no discussion of failure modes, scenarios where dense modeling helps minimally, or safety-critical near-miss cases; no investigation of model calibration assumptions underlying entropy-based uncertainty

Technical clarity issues: entropy-as-novelty assumes model calibration; claim about uncertainty reflecting 'distance to entire training distribution' needs stronger justification; assumptions about monocular depth consistency across scenes unvalidated
